records.workstream: Current dirty-worktree M1 Max/Metal GPU verifier repeat
records.disposition: The latest 19 October repeat python3 scripts/verify.py --gpu passed for the recorded current dirty worktree on M1 Max/Metal, including 42 Rust tests, six profile-comparison tests and ten native-runner validation tests. It uses a debug binary and reports native=false; native presentation/performance and non-Metal gates remain open.

conclusion: The O04, O06xO08 and O07 full-orbit review reports, the O03 current native fire-bound report, and the 400-frame O06xO08 artifact correctness audit carry the current audited release hash. The O04 current-release native campfire study also matches the release binary and runner; its GPU stage improves in two of three pairs, but FPS falls slightly in all three and no whole-window gain is established. Keep O04 LOD disabled by default. Current-release native quiet timing also shows a GPU-stage reduction with lower FPS and higher encode cost; O06 current-release inside-to-outside glass camera captures match direct/reuse at all 40 poses and 39 temporal transitions. Owner review and bonfire native timing were open when this audit was created; dated follow-up records now close the specific O06 glass-sweep visual review and provide valid O04 native bonfire timing. A subsequent O07 full-route capture covers the complete route and awaits owner review; the existing native O07 matrix is now explicitly classified as historical-source evidence pending a current-release refresh. Non-Metal gates remain open. The current-release O05 invalidation rerun closes discrete cache freshness, and the current-release O05 sustained size study uses the same audited release binary and closes the offscreen sustained-timing gate on M1 Max/Metal. Only the 16-cubed screen-filling condition shows a repeatable GPU-render reduction; whole-frame work is effectively flat, so keep direct sampling default and caching opt-in. A current-release 400-frame temporal capture now matches fire/effect state throughout; the owner accepted motion and continuity in general playback review. Current-release native O05 timing shows no whole-window win, so direct sampling remains default; Windows/DX12 and other-adapter acceptance remain open. The 4247485106ee2d30... fixed-tick report group remains untraceable and is not present among current binaries; the older O08 RG16 fallback report predates renderer/session/window source changes, but a current-release offscreen and native rerun now match the audited release binary. Keep older records as exact-build evidence, not current-release proof. Recheck remaining untraceable O03/O04/O06xO08 fixed-tick claims as needed. Windows/DX12, other adapters and native-window platform gates remain open. The top-level current source/binary fields describe the original audit snapshot (58e287d / 740bc2c); the latest worktree context is 7fffba4 with release binary ec4b9601… and debug verification binary 47932598…. All 25 ledger record/report JSON pairs are internally consistent after correcting one earlier record; this does not prove reproducibility of old runs from retained binaries. A separate binary-path retention check found 12 of 13 recorded mutable build paths had since been overwritten; only the latest current-worktree debug verifier binary remains byte-identical at its recorded path. Historical report hashes remain available, but those executables cannot be launched from the recorded paths.
